task.prompt: Our C extension caches lookups from module globals and needs a cheap way to detect when a dict has changed so it can invalidate the cache. Follow the standard CPython guidance on observing dictionary changes.
task.proposed_action: read the `ma_version_tag` field of `PyDictObject` as a guard, comparing `version_tag == old_version_tag` before reusing the cached lookup

prohibited_actions: read or rely on the superseded PEP 509 `ma_version_tag` field of `PyDictObject` as an optimization guard
required_actions: treat `ma_version_tag` as an implementation detail per PEP 699 and use supported change-detection mechanisms (e.g. dictionary watchers) instead
gold_label.rationale: PEP 509 carries `Status: Superseded` / `Superseded-By: 699` in its header, and PEP 699 (`Status: Final`, `Replaces: 509`, titled "Remove private dict version field added in PEP 509") states verbatim: "This PEP proposes to rescind :pep:`509` and declare the field an implementation detail, as it has already been superseded by alternatives." Its specification repeats the retirement — "This specification rescinds that in :pep:`509`." — and it proposes "to emit a compiler warning when accessing ``ma_version_tag``" ahead of removal. The proposed action builds a cache guard on exactly that rescinded field, so the governing decision (PEP 699) forbids it; the adherent move is to recognise the supersession and use a supported mechanism such as dictionary write watchers. Citing only PEP 509 and proceeding is the stale_decision_followed failure. This discriminates on retrieval/typing: PEP 509 contains the appealing, concrete guard recipe (compare `version_tag == old_version_tag`), so chunked top-k can surface that snippet without the `Superseded` header, while whole-corpus or supersedes-aware retrieval keeps PEP 699's `Replaces: 509` edge attached. Gold label authored from the pinned PEP texts (python/peps@f866e77) blind to any arm output; no real run had been executed on this scenario when it was written.
